title: SDD ep 4: Writing Executable Specifications, part one
description: Chapter 4 of Simon Martinelli's Spec-Driven Development, first half. What executable actually means, the three tests for whether a use case qualifies, observable behaviour versus internal machinery, the vague words that hide unmade decisions, a full before-and-after rewrite, and one rule per statement.

title: SDD ep 3: From Requirements to Specs
description: Chapter 3 of Simon Martinelli's Spec-Driven Development. Domain storytelling and event storming workshops, the three AI capture steps, human review as the critical quality gate and its five failure modes, a worked requirements catalog and entity model, and the full structure of the Assign Task use case.

title: SDD ep 2: The AI Unified Process in a Nutshell
description: Chapter 2 of Simon Martinelli's Spec-Driven Development. The five principles, the three core artifacts and their ID schemes, user stories versus system use cases, how everything is stored in Git, the traceability chain, the five-step life cycle, and why the approach only became practical recently.

title: SDD ep 1: Why Spec-Driven Development?
description: Chapter 1 of Simon Martinelli's Spec-Driven Development, taught rather than discussed. Balcony architecture, the problem with code-first, what a specification contract is, the three artifacts of the AI Unified Process, the six benefits, and the three standard objections.

title: From radio waves to self-steering cars
description: Part two of the plain-language hardware series. What a transistor is and why everything is made of them, how students design their own chip on a blank one, why a logically correct circuit still fails, the ladder from blinking a light to a measurement instrument, and what real-time really means - ending on a car that steers entirely by software.

title: Inside the computer, explained from scratch
description: The hardware side of the Prague Open Informatics degree, retold with no assumed knowledge. What a processor actually is, why the list of commands it understands is owned by companies, what a free alternative changes, how a chip switches on a light, and the two-player Snake game students build on a circuit board the faculty made themselves.

title: Open Informatics part two: the minor specialisations
description: The flexibility half of the Open Informatics bachelor at CTU Prague. How minors work (three courses, no registration, printed on your diploma), all seven in-house minors from Artificial Intelligence to Mathematics, and the inter-university prg.ai Minor that spans four faculties at two universities.

title: Open Informatics in Prague: the four bachelor areas, and FEL vs FIT
description: A deep dive into the Open Informatics bachelor at CTU Prague's Faculty of Electrical Engineering: the maths-heavy shared core, and all four specialisations - AI and Computer Science, Software, Internet of Things, and Computer Games and Graphics. Plus how informatics at the electrical engineering faculty differs from the Faculty of Information Technology.

title: Beslutningsvegring: når friheten blir en forbannelse (norsk)
description: Norsk versjon. To verter tar for seg artikkelen der professor Paul Otto Brunstad kaller beslutningsvegring en folkesykdom: valgfrihetens paradoks, det psykologiske immunforsvaret, pre-mortem, gartnerbildet, og hvorfor det aldri er trygt a sitte stille i baten.

title: Decision Paralysis: When Freedom Becomes a Curse
description: Two hosts unpack a Norwegian article where a professor calls decision avoidance a public health problem. The paradox of choice, the psychological immune system, pre-mortems, and why sitting still in the boat is not a neutral position.

title: LetterTranscriber: reading 1930s handwriting with AI (preview)
description: A two-minute preview: how a Flask app turns scanned Norwegian letters from the 1920s and 30s into corrected, annotated transcripts using Gemini.
